tools.name: list_public_conferences
tools.description: List the conferences published on Congressio — name, slug, dates, timezone, venue, organizer, and whether the program is published. Needs no credentials. Use this to answer 'which conferences are open', to find a conference by name, or to get the slug that get_public_conference needs. Returns only publicly visible conferences, so a user's own draft events will NOT appear here — use list_my_events for those.

offset.description: How many to skip, for paging.

tools.name: get_public_conference
tools.description: Fetch one publicly visible conference by its URL slug — dates, timezone, venue, organizer, program status, and the link to its public page. Needs no credentials. Use it once you have a slug, to answer detail questions about a specific conference; get the slug from list_public_conferences first. Returns an error for a conference that is draft, archived, or restricted to members.

slug.description: The conference's URL slug, as it appears in /events/<slug> and in list_public_conferences.

tools.name: list_my_events
tools.description: List every event belonging to the API key's organization, including drafts and archived ones, with their UUIDs. Use it to answer 'what events do we have' and as the first step before any other keyed tool: this is where you get the eventId that the submissions and registrations tools need — those take a UUID, not a slug. Requires the organization API key to be configured; without one this returns an error telling the user where to create a key. If the response includes a `links` object or a `dashboardUrl`, give the user the actual URL as a clickable link rather than describing where to click — they are in a chat, not in the product, and cannot navigate from a description.

tools.name: list_submissions
tools.description: List the papers and abstracts submitted to one of the organization's events, with each submission's review status and track. Use it to answer 'how many submissions do we have', 'what has been accepted', or to summarize a track. Draft and withdrawn submissions are excluded. Attendee registrations are NOT submissions — use list_registrations for those. Requires the organization API key to be configured; without one this returns an error telling the user where to create a key.

eventId.description: Event UUID from list_my_events — not the URL slug.

tools.name: get_submission
tools.description: Read a single paper in full: its title, track, status, the reviews written on it with each reviewer's scores and comments, the average per criterion, any rebuttal from the authors, the meta-review, and the decision if one has been recorded. Use it whenever the question is about a specific submission rather than a count — 'what did the reviewers say about this paper', 'why is this one scored low', 'is this ready to decide', or to summarize the reviews before recording a decision. Call list_submissions first to find the submission's id. Reviewer names and their comments to the organizers are included, so treat the result as confidential to the committee and do not quote the organizer-facing comments back to an author. Requires an OAuth connection rather than an API key, and the admin or committee role on the event — the same access the dashboard's decision queue needs.

eventId.description: Event UUID from list_my_events — not the URL slug.

tools.name: list_reviewers
tools.description: List everyone who reviews for one of the organization's conferences, with the tracks each covers, their free-text expertise, and how many reviews they are already carrying. Use it before assign_reviewer — that tool needs a reviewer's user id, and this is where to get it — and to answer 'who still has capacity', 'who knows about this topic', or 'who have we invited'. A reviewer with status 'invited' has a pending invitation and no account yet, so they cannot be assigned work until they sign up. Requires an OAuth connection and the admin or committee role on the event.

eventId.description: Event UUID from list_my_events — not the URL slug.

tools.name: list_tracks
tools.description: List the tracks (also called topics or categories) a conference accepts submissions under, with how many papers are in each. Use it to answer 'what tracks do we have', to summarize submissions by topic, or to find the track id that add_reviewer needs when recording a reviewer's expertise. Track names are also what list_submissions reports per paper, so this is how to see the full set rather than only the ones that happen to appear. Requires the organization API key to be configured; without one this returns an error telling the user where to create a key.

eventId.description: Event UUID from list_my_events — not the URL slug.

tools.name: list_forms
tools.description: List the forms attached to one of the organization's conferences — the call for papers, the registration form, and any decision forms — with how many questions each has and whether it is published. A form that is not published accepts nothing, so check this before concluding a conference is ready to receive submissions or registrations. Requires the organization API key to be configured; without one this returns an error telling the user where to create a key.

eventId.description: Event UUID from list_my_events — not the URL slug.

tools.name: create_call_for_papers
tools.description: Create the submission form authors fill in — the questions a call for papers asks, such as a title, an abstract, a track and a file upload. Use it after create_draft_conference, because a conference with no submission form has nothing for anyone to submit to. Pass the questions as a simple list; each needs a label and a type (text, paragraph, rich_text, choice, multi_choice, checkbox, file, date, number, email), and choice and multi_choice also need options. IMPORTANT — the form is created as a DRAFT and accepts nothing until a human publishes it in the dashboard, so tell the user that submissions are not open yet and that they must publish it and then set the submission window. This creates a simple question list; pages, sections, conditional logic and layout are done in the dashboard's form builder afterwards. Requires an OAuth connection and the admin role on the event. If the response includes a `links` object or a `dashboardUrl`, give the user the actual URL as a clickable link rather than describing where to click — they are in a chat, not in the product, and cannot navigate from a description.

eventId.description: Event UUID from list_my_events — not the URL slug.

name.description: What the form is called, e.g. "Call for Papers".

label.description: The question as the author will read it.

type.description: What kind of answer this question takes.

required.description: Whether an author must answer it. Defaults to false.

options.description: The choices, for a choice or multi_choice question. Required for those two types.

description.description: Help text shown under the question.

questions.description: The questions, in the order authors will see them.

tools.name: list_registrations
tools.description: List the confirmed attendees of one of the organization's events — name, email, ticket tier, and whether the registration is paid. Use it to answer 'how many people are coming', to check whether someone is registered, or to summarize ticket sales. Unfinished (draft) registrations are excluded. Returns attendee personal data, so do not paste it anywhere the user did not ask for. Requires the organization API key to be configured; without one this returns an error telling the user where to create a key.

eventId.description: Event UUID from list_my_events — not the URL slug.

tools.name: register_attendee
tools.description: Register one attendee for an event and issue their QR pass — the programmatic equivalent of a walk-up registration, useful for importing someone from another system. It does NOT take payment and does not raise an invoice: the registration is created as comped. Confirm the name and email with the user before calling this, because the attendee may be emailed. Calling it twice for the same person is safe: the existing registration is returned instead of creating a second one. Requires the organization API key to be configured; without one this returns an error telling the user where to create a key.

eventId.description: Event UUID from list_my_events — not the URL slug.

name.description: The attendee's full name, as it should appear on the badge.

email.description: The attendee's email. An existing account with this address is reused; otherwise a passwordless one is created.

tier.description: Ticket tier — the value or label of an option on the event's registration form. Omit to register without a tier.

tools.name: create_draft_conference
tools.description: Create a new conference as a DRAFT — it is not publicly visible until someone publishes it in Congressio, so this is safe to use while still deciding details. Use it when the user wants to start organising a new conference. Needs a name and an IANA timezone (for example Europe/Paris); dates are optional and can be added later in the UI. Confirm the name, timezone and dates with the user before calling, since the draft appears in their organization immediately. Returns the new conference's id and slug. This tool requires an OAuth connection rather than an API key, because a created conference records who created it — with an API key it returns a 403 explaining that. It can also fail with 402 if the organization's plan has no room for another active conference, which is not something retrying will fix. Requires the organization API key to be configured; without one this returns an error telling the user where to create a key.

name.description: The conference name, as attendees will see it.

timezone.description: IANA timezone, e.g. Europe/Paris. Dates are interpreted in it, so ask the user rather than guessing.

startDate.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD). Must not be in the past.

endDate.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD). Must not be before startDate.

tools.name: update_conference
tools.description: Change a conference's name, dates, venue or URL slug. Send only what changes — anything omitted is left as it is, and an empty string clears an optional field. Use it when the user wants to correct or fill in details of a conference that already exists; get the eventId from list_my_events first. Dates are calendar days in the conference's own timezone, so "2027-06-01" means that date locally. Changing the slug changes the public URL, so confirm that with the user before doing it. Requires the user to be an admin of that specific conference — being an owner of the organization is not enough, and a 403 says so. Needs an OAuth connection rather than an API key. Requires the organization API key to be configured; without one this returns an error telling the user where to create a key.

eventId.description: Event UUID from list_my_events — not the URL slug.

slug.description: Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. Changes the public URL — confirm first.

startDate.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD), in the conference's timezone.

tools.name: set_conference_windows
tools.description: Set when the call for papers and registration open and close. Use it to open a CFP, extend a deadline, or close registration. Send only the bounds you are changing. IMPORTANT: null and omitted mean different things — pass null to REMOVE a deadline (leaving that window open with no end), and omit the field entirely to leave it as it is. So "reopen the CFP" means passing submissionClose: null, not an empty call. A close date must be after its matching open date. Opening a CFP has a real effect: authors can submit from that moment, so confirm the dates with the user first. Returns the merged stored windows, which answers "is the CFP open now?" directly. Requires the user to be an admin of that specific conference, and an OAuth connection rather than an API key. Requires the organization API key to be configured; without one this returns an error telling the user where to create a key.

eventId.description: Event UUID from list_my_events — not the URL slug.

submissionOpen.description: ISO 8601 date-time when the CFP opens, or null to remove the bound. Omit to leave unchanged.

submissionClose.description: ISO 8601 submission deadline, or null to remove it (CFP stays open). Omit to leave unchanged.

tools.name: publish_conference
tools.description: Publish a DRAFT conference so it becomes publicly visible: it appears in the directory, its pages resolve, and its call for papers opens to authors. No emails are sent. This is the first irreversible-feeling step, so always confirm with the user before calling it. IMPORTANT two-step behaviour: call it first WITHOUT acknowledgeMissing. If required setup is incomplete the conference is NOT published and you get back a list of what is missing — relay that list to the user in plain language and ask whether to publish anyway. Only if they say yes, call again passing those exact keys as acknowledgeMissing. Never invent or guess those keys: if they do not match what is actually missing the call is refused. A conference that is already live returns an error saying so. Requires the organization API key to be configured; without one this returns an error telling the user where to create a key.

eventId.description: Event UUID from list_my_events — not the URL slug.

acknowledgeMissing.description: ONLY the setup item keys a previous call reported as missing, copied verbatim after the user agreed to publish anyway. Omit on the first call.

tools.name: add_reviewer
tools.description: Give someone the reviewer role for a conference, by email address. Use it when the user wants to bring a reviewer onto their programme committee. IMPORTANT and easy to get wrong: this does NOT send anyone an email. If the address already belongs to a verified Congressio account the person becomes a reviewer immediately; otherwise a pending invitation is recorded and activates only when they sign up with that exact address. The response says which happened — relay it accurately, and if it was an invitation tell the user they still need to contact the person themselves. Do not report "I've invited them" as though a message went out. Confirm the address with the user before calling, since a typo grants nothing and silently waits. Requires the user to be an admin of that conference, and an OAuth connection rather than an API key. Requires the organization API key to be configured; without one this returns an error telling the user where to create a key.

eventId.description: Event UUID from list_my_events — not the URL slug.

email.description: The reviewer's email address. Confirm it with the user first.

categoryIds.description: Track or category ids to scope this reviewer to. Omit to let them review across all tracks.

tools.name: assign_reviewer
tools.description: Assign one of the conference's reviewers to review one submission. Use it when the user is distributing papers to their programme committee. This EMAILS the reviewer to tell them they have a paper to review, so confirm the pairing with the user before calling. Get the submissionId from list_submissions and make sure the person is already a reviewer (add_reviewer does that). The platform will refuse the assignment — and you should relay the reason rather than retrying — if the reviewer has a declared conflict of interest with that submission, is its submitter, is one of its co-authors, is already assigned to it, or has hit their maximum review load. Those are facts about the people involved, not problems with your request, so the answer is to suggest a different reviewer. It will also refuse if the conference has no review stage configured yet — that is set up in the dashboard under the Review settings, and no assignment can exist before it. Requires the user to be an admin of that conference, and an OAuth connection rather than an API key. Requires the organization API key to be configured; without one this returns an error telling the user where to create a key.

eventId.description: Event UUID from list_my_events — not the URL slug.

reviewerId.description: The reviewer's user id. They must already be a reviewer for this conference.

tools.name: record_decision
tools.description: Record an accept, reject or revise outcome on a single paper, optionally with private notes and feedback for the author. Use it after get_submission, when working through papers one at a time: read the reviews, decide, move on. IMPORTANT — this does NOT email anyone. The decision is saved privately and the author cannot see it. Always tell the user that nothing has been sent, and that to actually send decisions they must either open the event's Decisions page in Congressio and use "Finalize all", or ask you to run release_decisions, which emails every author at once and cannot be undone. Recording a decision can be repeated to change it while it is unsent. Pass the decision type's name as configured on the event, such as "Accept" or "Reject"; if you get it wrong the error lists the valid names. Requires an OAuth connection and the admin role on the event. If the response includes a `links` object or a `dashboardUrl`, give the user the actual URL as a clickable link rather than describing where to click — they are in a chat, not in the product, and cannot navigate from a description.

eventId.description: Event UUID from list_my_events — not the URL slug.

submissionId.description: Submission UUID from list_submissions or get_submission.

decision.description: The decision type's name as configured on this event, e.g. "Accept", "Reject", "Minor revision".

notes.description: Private notes for the organizers. The author never sees these.

authorFeedback.description: Feedback the author WILL see — but only once decisions are released, not now.

tools.name: release_decisions
tools.description:
⚠️ THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL TOOL HERE. Finalises the draft accept/reject decisions for a conference and SENDS AN EMAIL TO EVERY AFFECTED AUTHOR. Emails cannot be recalled. For many authors this is the message that decides whether they travel. Nothing else in this tool set contacts anyone outside the organizer's own data.

MANDATORY TWO STEPS — do not skip the first:
  1. Call with ONLY eventId. Nothing is sent. You get back a count of how many authors WOULD be emailed, plus any submissions still lacking a decision or short of reviews.
  2. Tell the user that exact number, say plainly that it cannot be undone, and ask them to confirm. Do not assume, do not infer consent from an earlier instruction like "finish the reviews", and do not proceed on a vague yes.
  3. Only if they explicitly agree, call again with confirmAuthorsToEmail set to that exact number.

Do NOT guess the number: a wrong one is refused, and if the decisions changed since you looked the stale number is refused too, so you must re-read and re-confirm. A count of 0 still needs the confirmation step. Requires the user to be an admin of that conference, and an OAuth connection rather than an API key. Requires the organization API key to be configured; without one this returns an error telling the user where to create a key.

eventId.description: Event UUID from list_my_events — not the URL slug.

confirmAuthorsToEmail.description: ONLY after step 1 reported this exact count AND the user explicitly agreed to send. Omit on the first call. Never a number you worked out yourself.

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description:
Send the user's feedback about Congressio's AI connector to the Congressio team — what worked, what was confusing, what a tool got wrong. Use it when the user expresses frustration with the connector itself, says a tool did the wrong thing, or asks how to report a problem. Do not send feedback the user did not ask you to send, and send their words rather than your summary of them.

ATTACHING THE CONVERSATION IS SEPARATE AND NEEDS AN EXPLICIT YES. The conversation contains their conference data — unreleased decisions, reviewer comments written for organizers, attendee names and email addresses. Before setting transcriptConsent, ask them in these terms: "Would you like me to include our conversation so far? It would let the Congressio team see exactly what happened, but it contains your conference data, including any decisions, reviewer comments or attendee details we discussed." Only set transcriptConsent true if they clearly agree. If they decline, do not answer, or you are unsure, send the feedback without a transcript — it is still useful. Never attach a transcript to feedback the user did not ask you to send.

Afterwards, tell them what was sent, whether the conversation was included, and that they can email privacy@congressio.net to have it deleted. Requires the organization API key to be configured; without one this returns an error telling the user where to create a key.

message.description: The user's feedback, in their own words.

toolName.description: Which tool the problem was about, if there was one — e.g. 'create_call_for_papers'.

transcript.description: The conversation, ONLY if the user explicitly agreed to share it. Send the part that shows the problem rather than the whole history.

transcriptConsent.description: True only when the user has been asked, in the terms described above, and clearly said yes. Required if transcript is set; the request is refused otherwise.

tools.name: read_documentation
tools.description: Read Congressio's own documentation as Markdown. Call with no slug for the index of every guide, then with a slug for one page (for example 'api-webhooks', 'call-for-papers', 'reviewing', 'registration'). Use this before answering a how-do-I question about the product rather than guessing — the docs are the authority on what the platform actually does. Needs no credentials.

slug.description: A documentation page slug. Omit to get the index listing every page and its slug.
